// diagnostic

E1010

An `[U8]{"…"}` binary pattern matched against a subject that isn't `[U8]` (D-BINPAT1 / D-UNIFYLIT1)

What

An `[U8]{"…"}` binary pattern matched against a subject that isn't `[U8]` (D-BINPAT1 / D-UNIFYLIT1)

Why

The registered sema rule applies here

Fix

Follow the guidance for E1010

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1010: tests/ui/binpat_subject_not_bytes.stderr.

Error [E1010]: this pattern matches raw bytes, but the subject is String (text)
  --> tests/ui/binpat_subject_not_bytes.jet:4:9
    |
  4 |         [U8]{"{x:U8}"} -> { print("x") }
    |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: an `[U8].{"…"}` binary pattern only matches a `[U8]` byte buffer
 Fix: match a `[U8]` subject, or use a pattern for this type instead
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1010

Error [E0116]: `print` doesn't hand back a value
  --> tests/ui/binpat_subject_not_bytes.jet:4:29
    |
  4 |         [U8]{"{x:U8}"} -> { print("x") }
    |                             ^^^^^
 Why: a call is a value only when its function declares a result after the parameter list
 Fix: inside an arm, wrap the call in `{ … }`; otherwise put `print` on its own line, or declare it as `fn print(…) Type -> …`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0116

Error [E0116]: `print` doesn't hand back a value
  --> tests/ui/binpat_subject_not_bytes.jet:6:13
    |
  6 |             print("no")
    |             ^^^^^
 Why: a call is a value only when its function declares a result after the parameter list
 Fix: inside an arm, wrap the call in `{ … }`; otherwise put `print` on its own line, or declare it as `fn print(…) Type -> …`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0116
